content.title: About
content.content: Passion fruit (Passiflora edulis) is a tropical fruit with aromatic sweet‑tart pulp filled with numerous edible seeds. The fruit grows in South America, Africa, Asia and the Caribbean. It is eaten fresh or used in juices, desserts, sauces and marinades.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Passion fruit belongs to the Passifloraceae family and is related to kiwi and pears.
The seeds are rich in dietary fiber and antioxidants.
The dark‑green rind changes color from yellow to purple depending on the variety.
In traditional medicine the fruit is used to aid digestion and reduce anxiety.
Passion fruit juice is a popular ingredient in cocktails, ice cream and meat marinades.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and helps synthesize collagen.

items.title: Contains vitamin A and carotenoids
items.content: These nutrients help maintain healthy vision and skin.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes normal digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium help regulate blood pressure and support heart function.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to passion fruit.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Seed hardness
items.content: Seeds are hard; they should be ground or avoided for young children to prevent choking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the fruit in half and scoop out the pulp with a spoon. The juice can be added to smoothies, cocktails, sauces and desserts. Seeds can be mixed into yogurt, oatmeal or baked goods for a crunchy texture.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store passion fruit in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, where it will keep for up to 2 weeks. Ripe fruits are best used within a few days. Discard any fruit with soft spots or off‑odors.
